newsitem.title: FRANCE: French car stocks up on restructuring hopes.
newsitem.headline: French car stocks up on restructuring hopes.

text.p: Shares in Renault SA and PSA Peugeot-Citroen were sharply higher on Friday as investors reacted to news that Renault would close a plant in Belgium and cut some 3,100 jobs, a move seen as the start of a restructuring in France's car industry.

French broker Chevreux de Virieu upgraded Renault to a buy rating from a sell, saying the plant closure would produce about 700 million francs in savings next year and that a more far-reaching restructuring could produce savings of up to two billion francs.
NatWest Sellier suspended its lighten rating on Renault and said it wanted to know more about any restructuring at the firm.
Renault was up 9.77 percent at 142.7 francs at 1129 GMT, after having earlier risen as high as 150 francs.
Peugeot was up 6.81 percent at 627 francs, off its earlier high of 645 francs.
On Friday morning, French finance minister Jean Arthuis said in a radio interview that French carmakers would have to restructure if they wanted to compete in an international market.
